title: TypeScript Is Killing JavaScript (And It's a Problem)

script.hook: Bhai, JavaScript mar raha hai — aur TypeScript uska murderer hai. Aur kuch log isko celebration maan rahe hain!
script.body:
Suno, TypeScript ne 2024 mein 78% developer adoption cross kar liya — Stack Overflow survey mein top 3 most-loved language ban gaya. Bada achievement hai, lekin problem kya hai?

Problem yeh hai ki ab junior devs directly TypeScript seekh rahe hain — bina JavaScript ki foundation samjhe. Ek building bana rahe ho bina neev ke.

TypeScript sirf JavaScript ka superset hai — uske bina TypeScript ek single line compile nahi hoti. Types hatao, neeche vanilla JS hi milega. Toh agar JS weak hai tumhari, toh TS bhi hollow hai.

Aur companies? Unhe lagta hai TypeScript = better code. But type safety sirf ek tool hai — sochne ki ability replace nahi karta. Strict mode off karke any type daalte hain aur kehte hain 'TypeScript use kar rahe hain' — yeh toh cheating hai!
script.cta: Comment mein batao — pehle JavaScript seekhi thi ya seedha TypeScript? Aur agar yeh video ne kuch naya dikhaya, toh follow karo CodeOrCap ko. Stop Guessing. Start Knowing.

metadata.title: TypeScript Is Killing JavaScript (And It's a Problem)
metadata.description:
JavaScript mar raha hai — aur TypeScript uska murderer hai. Aur kuch log isko celebration maan rahe hain! But is that really a good thing for the developer community?

In this video, we break down why TypeScript has exploded in popularity across every major tech company, what it's actually replacing (hint: it's more than just JavaScript), and the hidden cost nobody is talking about — slower onboarding, complex build tooling, and a rapidly rising barrier for new developers trying to enter the field.

We cover:
• Why companies are forcing TypeScript on every new project
• What TypeScript gets RIGHT — and where it goes too far
• Is JavaScript actually dying or just evolving?
• Should YOU switch to TypeScript in 2025?

Whether you're a JavaScript loyalist or a full TypeScript convert, this video will challenge how you think about modern web development.
